          Goals at a 60-Year High, Swans Flying, and Burnley's Breakdown: The Championship's Biggest Early-Season Storylines
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Following an extended break for international football, the Championship returns this weekend. After almost three weeks off, here‘s a recap of the need-to-know stats before the action gets back under way.
There have already been 277 goals scored in the Championship in 2026-27, with this the highest total after eight matchdays of a season since 2012-13 (295).
With 95 games played, the goals-per-game average is 2.92, higher than any full Championship season since the competition rebranded in 2004-05 (the highest for a completed season is 2.74 in 2010-11).
In fact, this is currently the highest goals-per-game average the second tier in England has witnessed since 1966-67 (2.95).

West Ham lead the way in the goalscoring stakes, with 22 goals after eight games. That equals Coventry City’s tally at this stage last season. The previous team before them to score that many goals after eight matches in the Championship was QPR in 2010-11 (22). The only team to score more after eight games in a season than West Ham since the Championship rebrand in 2004-05 were Wolves in 2008-09 (23).
All three of those sides went on to win the league title that season – that's certainly a good omen for the Hammers.

Swansea City sit top of the Championship table as we return to action following the extended international break. It’s the first time that Swansea have been top of the league this late into a season since October 2019, when they eventually finished sixth and lost in the play-off semis.

Their tally of 17 points is quite low for a league leader after eight games of a season. Across 22 years of the Championship since it rebranded in 2004-05, this is just the eighth occasion that a team have been top of the league with 17 points or fewer, with only one of those teams having a lower points total – Brighton in 2012-13 (16).

Swansea have been winning for the biggest proportion of match time in the Championship this season (44.2%) and will hope to keep their strong form going in order to earn a spot back in the Premier League for the first time since their relegation in 2017-18.

Interestingly, while there are 10 points and 20 places between Swansea and rivals Cardiff City in the real Championship table, Opta’s expected points table places Cardiff a spot above the Swans (7th vs 8th). That suggests Swansea’s current league position is slightly inflated compared to their underlying performances at both ends of the pitch.

There’s no doubt that boss Vitor Matos has turned his side into one of the most intense teams out of possession in the attacking half, though. They rank first in the Championship for possession won in the final third (40) and lead the league rankings for total high turnovers (70) as well as shots (16) and goals (3) from high turnovers too.
The jump from League One to the Championship feels small compared to that of the Championship to the Premier League.

While teams promoted from the Championship have struggled to compete overall in the top flight over recent seasons, the same can’t be said for teams that were promoted from the third tier to the second tier.

Since 2022-23, just one of 12 promoted teams has been relegated back to League One in the first season as a Championship club. That team were Wigan Athletic in 2022-23, and the Latics did have a six-point deduction, but that didn’t end up making a difference.
We’re potentially on course for a fourth successive Championship season without a single promoted side being relegated back to League One.

Last season saw as many as two promoted clubs finish inside the top half of the Championship table – Wrexham in 7th and Birmingham City in 10th – for the first time since 2017-18, and there’s every chance that feat might be achieved again.

Lincoln City (11) and Bolton Wanderers (10) have reached double-figures for points already and sit around mid-table, while Cardiff are just above the relegation zone on seven points. Both Cardiff (7th) and Lincoln (9th) are inside the top 10 for expected points, however.

Before this season, Burnley’s last four appearances in the Championship have all ended in automatic promotion at the end of the campaign (2013-14, 2015-16, 2022-23 and 2024-25). The last two of those have seen them accrue 100+ points – the only club to reach a century of points more than once in the second tier in history.
In basic terms, when Burnley have been a Championship club, we’re used to seeing them at the top of the table. But not this time.

The Clarets sit bottom of the table after eight matchdays and are the only team without a win in the Championship. Their tally of four points is their lowest after eight games of a season outside the top flight since 1997-98 in the second tier (also 4), when they ended the season 20th.
